question: Summarize the page about the 2021 NBA Finals.
raw_answer: The 2021 NBA Finals was the championship series of the NBA's 2020–21 season, contested between the Eastern Conference champion Milwaukee Bucks and the Western Conference champion Phoenix Suns [4]. The series took place from July 6 to July 20, 2021 [1]. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Phoenix Suns in six games, winning the series 4–2 [1][6], securing their first NBA championship in 50 years and their second overall [4]. The Bucks won the final four games of the series after losing the first two games on the road [4]. Giannis Antetokounmpo, the Bucks' forward, was named NBA Finals Most Valuable Player (MVP) [1][3][5], recognizing his performance throughout the series, including a historic 50-point, 14-rebound, 5-block effort in Game 6 [5]. The series was broadcast by Mike Breen, Mark Jackson, and Jeff Van Gundy, with Malika Andrews replacing Rachel Nichols as sideline reporter [4]. The Finals were the first since 2010 without LeBron James or Stephen Curry, the first since 1998 without a team from California, Texas, or Florida, and the first since 1984 without a teammate of Shaquille O'Neal [4]. The average American audience for the series was 9.91 million viewers [4].

The **2021 NBA Finals** was the championship series of the National Basketball Association's (NBA) 2020–21 season and conclusion of the season's playoffs. In this best-of-seven playoff series, the Eastern Conference champion Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Western Conference champion Phoenix Suns, 4–2, winning their first NBA championship in 50 years and second overall. Holding home-court advantage, the Suns led the series 2–0 before the Bucks won the next four games, becoming the fifth team in NBA history to win the championship after losing the first two games. Milwaukee's Giannis Antetokounmpo was named NBA Finals Most Valuable Player (MVP).<sup>[1]</sup> With the COVID-19 pandemic altering the NBA's schedule for the second consecutive year, the start date of the series was pushed from its usual time in late May or early June to July 6, the second-latest start in Finals' history. This was the first NBA Finals since 2010 to have neither LeBron James nor Stephen Curry as one of the players competing, the first since 1998 to not feature a team from California, Texas, or Florida, as well as the first Finals since 1984 to not feature a teammate of Shaquille O'Neal.

As with the previous years, the series was called by Mike Breen on play-by-play with Mark Jackson and Jeff Van Gundy as analysts. Rachel Nichols was originally to be the sideline reporter, but Malika Andrews took over due to a leaked audio of Nichols saying racist comments against Maria Taylor.<sup>[68]</sup>
